observations: CORRECTION IMPACT: the ORIGINAL Scan B session's p34.json entry mixed two different things -- it correctly captured this page's HEADER phrase ('ראשון המובב עלינו... צפונית מערבית') and its DIAGRAM, but the running body text attached to that header actually belongs to PDF page 34 (the Marah/Elim discourse, now corrected in this batch's own p34.json). This page's OWN body text -- Yesod as world-ruler, the Sabbath 'zachor/shamor' seventh/tenth-measure discourse, and the king's-betrothed/king's-sons-bread parables -- was not captured by the original session at all.

The 'king and his betrothed, available one day a week' parable is a notable early attestation of the Sabbath-as-bride motif, worth flagging as a substantive literary-historical data point distinct from any of the extraction categories' narrow definitions.
This page's Yesod-as-'sar shel kol olam' (prince of the whole world, sustaining 'nefesh kol chai') is a clean, quotable proto-sefirotic statement.
